active.title: context dead --snapshot pauses open worktrees: archive/wt tag for a private repo, local bundle for a public one
active.description: Measured (HEAD e83e55783): `dead` refuses while any `wt/*` worktree of the context is open (`_dead_preflight`, `features/spec_context/service.py:679-692`, from `worktree_rows` and `GitSubprocessClient.unrecoverable`, `infrastructure/git_subprocess.py:244-266`; ADR 0128 layer 4), so work in flight cannot be paused; the exits are merge or clean only (ADRs 0099, 0128 layer 1); `alive` (`service.py:462-529`) knows nothing of worktrees. The pre-push already scans tags and skips branch policy for them (`features/chokepoints/push_gate.py:176-189`). Change: path 1 = merge (exists); path 2 = `context dead --snapshot`: an identity preflight (`GitSubprocessClient.identity_fix`) refuses before anything is touched -> per open `wt/*` a WIP commit on its branch that stages only that worktree (untracked included, ignored never; never `repos/<r>`) -> the same denylist+baseline scan the pre-push runs -> visibility by `gh repo view --json visibility` (unknown = public): private -> tag `archive/wt/<ctx>/<repo>/<name>` pushed to origin (never a branch, ADR 0120); public or unknown -> `git bundle` at `.dadaia/snapshots/<ctx>/<repo>/<name>.bundle` with a 'not portable' warning, in a new durable zone `.dadaia/snapshots/` (no TTL; a bundle leaves only when `alive` restores it or by an explicit verb; `export --hard` packs it from there; `.dadaia/reaped/` and the reaper gain no special case; ADR 0112, nothing is deleted by time) -> the worktree is removed. `alive` lists the context's snapshots and prints the restore `fix:` in the new layout. For `wt/*` trees the snapshot replaces the preflight's per-worktree refusal lines; a foreign worktree keeps its refusal. ADD justified: no unit carries pausing; it reuses the archive tag (ADR 0120), the push scan and `identity_fix`; its only new surface is the `snapshots` zone. Done when: dead with an open worktree in a public and in a private repo finishes losing no byte (the tag or the bundle restores the tree, untracked files included), and nothing of a public repo leaves the machine. Files: features/spec_context/service.py (dead, alive), infrastructure/git_subprocess.py (unrecoverable), features/chokepoints (scan, reused), dd-gitflow-default/scripts/_worktree_end.py, cli/commands/context.py, core/workspace_layout.py (the new `snapshots` zone in `DADAIA_ZONES`), public/data/dadaia-AGENTS.md (the zone row of `.dadaia/AGENTS.md`). Bugs (same mechanisms reused, must not regress): dead-commit-fails-without-git-identity (the WIP commit is the one commit dead still authors: identity preflight first), context-alive-sweeps-unrelated-worktree-changes (the WIP commit stages only the archived worktree), unrecoverable-fix-line-pushes-a-wt-branch-the-pre-push-refuses, sa-context-dead-removes-repos-outside-the-reaper, reaper-deletes-linked-git-worktrees. ADR 0173 (proposed; amends 0120 at acceptance).

active.description: Measured (HEAD e83e55783): `dadaia export` (`features/export/service.py`) writes `.dadaia/dist/spec-contexts.json` (`spec-contexts-export-v1`) with contexts and the main repo's branch only, and rewrites the registry as a side effect (`_refresh_branches`, `:49-63`, `self._store.update` at `:59`); it knows no harness and no WIP; this instance's artifact dates from 0.4.5 (2026-09-04). Scope narrowed by SPEC 0.4.6 D12/D15 (tar retired, f4bf7e0b2); no ADR covers export. Change: export is read-only (delete `_refresh_branches` and its `_store.update`); soft (default) `.dadaia/dist/spec-contexts.json` schema v2: contexts (slug, name, state, main repo url, associated [{slug,url}]), the exact `dadaia_version`, the harnesses of `.dadaia/states/harness_profile.json`, per repo its snapshots (tags portable; bundles listed as not portable, warning exit); hard `dadaia export --hard` -> one `.tar.gz` in `.dadaia/dist/` = soft + bundles of every open worktree and every bundle of `.dadaia/snapshots/`, content passed through the denylist+baseline scan (a hit refuses); never the denylist, credentials, sessions or the install ledger. The `dist` zone (`core/workspace_layout.py:194`) admits both. The artifact reader is hardened: an incomplete record -> DadaiaError, a null url refused. ADD justified: the hard artifact is the one carrier of local-only work (a public repo's bundle never leaves by git). It does not resurrect the retired tar pipeline's bug class (import-extracts-manifest-to-root): one archive of fixed members (the soft JSON and `snapshots/<ctx>/<repo>/<name>.bundle`); every member validated before extraction (no absolute path, no `..`, no link, nothing outside that list); the JSON is read in memory and extraction is confined to `.dadaia/snapshots/`, never the root. Done when: soft and hard validate against their schemas; a hard export with a planted secret is refused. Files: features/export/service.py, cli/commands/export.py, core/models/spec_context.py (EXPORT_SCHEMA_VERSION), core/workspace_layout.py (dist zone), the artifact reader, public/schemas (two new schemas). Bugs (class guarded): import-extracts-manifest-to-root (a restored archive lands outside its zone), import-export-workspace-flag-re-resolves-through-ancestor-walk (export half), context-create-admits-uncloneable-empty-url (the null-url class). ADR 0211 answered with a tier cut (the stage level runs lint, typecheck, guards and the whole small tier); the rc-10 Reconciliation review (M3) found that cut is an agent reading of the demand, not the mapping the operator asked for, and deferred it here. Design: the local stage gate and worktree.py merge derive the selection from the change itself - the static import graph of the changed modules (a test is selected when it imports, transitively, a changed module) united with the owner tests the job file declares per task (task-gate-declared-owner-tests is that mapping's one decider; no second owner list); a change the graph cannot resolve (law, data, schema, a non-Python file) selects the whole small tier; CI on push keeps the full suite of every tier unchanged, so a selection miss surfaces there, never as a skip. One decider for the selection, in scripts/ci.py; no new marker. Placement and every design detail not quoted from a ruling are agent default, unruled.

active.title: Existing code migrates to the multi-platform-by-construction ADR, rules P1-P10, one sweep per rule
active.description: Operator, 2026-10-07, verbatim: 'toda arquitetura e a forma como metodos são programados deve pensar em ser multi-plataforma'; 'tanto na lib, na CLI, nos scripts dentro de skills'; ADR accepted the same day: 'Aceito, com essa divisão (Recommended)'. The ADR has no id yet: decisions.jsonl on feature/0.5.0 and every rc-10 tree carries no multi-platform record (the rc-10 Reconciliation writes it through its lane). Decision: one codebase; OS facts live in one seam, dadaia_workspace/core/platform.py, and tooling refuses OS literals elsewhere. Rules: P1 platform.py is the only reader of sys.platform/os.name, venv dir and .exe via sysconfig; P2 never bare python/bash - sys.executable, executables via shutil.which; P3 list argv, shell=False, no shlex; P4 pathlib in code, as_posix only for display/compare, no '/' joins; P5 encoding='utf-8' on all text I/O incl. hook stdout, CI never masks with PYTHONUTF8; P6 rmtree onexc read-only handler, os.replace atomic writes, no exec bit/symlink reliance; P7 one renderer for printed commands (core/cli_line), never &&, $VAR, sudo, chmod +x; P8 git and harness hooks are a one-line #!/bin/sh shim exec'ing the absolute interpreter, logic in Python; P9 shipped law names commands once, neutral, rendered per platform at install; P10 ruff PTH, S602, S605, PLW1514, a guard refusing OS literals outside the seam, Windows+macOS CI = Linux selection, .gitattributes eol. Split (ruled): rc-10 bug batch takes the 8 Windows bugs, shipped-law-hardcodes-the-posix-venv-path (P9) and CI selection parity (P10 CI part); this entry is the rc-11 rest - hook shims (P8), pre-push in Python, lint + guard (P10), path joins (P4), one command renderer (P7). Design: one sweep per P-rule over dadaia_workspace/ (lib, CLI, skill scripts), each sweep lands with its repo guard (the P10 OS-literal guard or the named ruff rule) turned on in the same job so the rule cannot regress; each sweep's commit carries its git grep line and hit count. Open (to the PLAN): how skill scripts get command lines without a second decider - relay the CLI's rendered output. Placement rc-11 is the operator's split; every other design detail not quoted from a ruling is agent default, unruled.

active.title: The merge gate knows who wrote a verdict, and a PR-edge verdict binds a hash
active.description: rc-10 Reconciliation review, deferred: 'the merge gate cannot tell who ran verdict.py; a PR-edge verdict reads no hash'. What Job 10 covers (SPEC AC12.2, ADR 0218): the verdict carries reviewed_sha and diff_sha256 and worktree.py merge refuses a missing field or a mismatch - a verdict binds the diff. What it leaves (SPEC 2026-10-07 amendment: 'authorship stays discipline plus audit, backlog verdict-author-unbound'): (1) authorship - any session, the merging main thread included, can run verdict.py over the right range and produce a hash-valid verdict, so the 'main thread never writes a verdict' rule of ADR 0218 is unenforced; (2) the PR edge - the work->integration and integration->principal verdicts are the reviewer's text pasted by the main thread into the PR, bound to no sha and no hash. Design: (1) the PreToolUse gate refuses a Bash run of verdict.py whose hook payload does not come from a dd-code-reviewer subagent (the payload's agent type is the one decider), with an adversary test where the main thread runs verdict.py itself; where a harness carries no agent type, the gate fails open and the audit counts verdicts with no reviewer session; (2) verdict.py gains a PR mode that hashes the PR's base..head diff, and the PR quote carries reviewed_sha and diff_sha256 so the promote reads the same binding the merge gate reads - one verdict shape, one decider. Placement and every design detail not quoted from a ruling are agent default, unruled.
